01 / THE LIFECYCLE

Background work.
Foreground control.

Use the same CLI across projects and agent sessions. Every service has an owner label, a deadline and a place in your process list.

  1. 01

    Start with a lease

    Wrap the foreground command you already use. ProcLease supervises its process group in the caller’s execution context.

    proclease run --ttl 2h -- npm run dev
  2. 02

    See what’s alive

    One terminal view for deadlines, CPU and resident memory. Bounded logs and JSON keep later tool calls informed.

    proclease watch
  3. 03

    Extend, stop, or expire

    Add time explicitly when work continues. Otherwise the deadline triggers TERM, then KILL after the shutdown grace.

    proclease extend JOB_ID --by 1h

02 / SMALL BY DESIGN

Local supervision.
Explicit deadlines.

A focused local tool for the dev server an agent starts and everyone forgets. No hosted service needed to run the CLI.

Reads don’t renew
Checking status, logs or resources leaves the lease unchanged.
History stays bounded
Up to five completions stay visible for 30 seconds. Finished history is retained for 24 hours or the newest 100 jobs.
Control stays explicit
Jobs are supervised individually. No shared service accepts arbitrary commands from another execution context.

05 / KNOW THE BOUNDARY

A few details
before you run.

Will it find servers I already started?+

ProcLease manages services launched through proclease run. It doesn’t adopt existing PIDs. A skill helps the agent choose ProcLease for future launches.

Does closing watch stop my services?+

No. Ctrl+C closes the terminal view. A job stops on explicit stop, command exit, expiry or supervision failure. Status and log reads never extend the deadline.

What do CPU and RSS include?+

The service and children still in its managed process group, excluding ProcLease supervisors. CPU 100% is one core. RSS sums resident bytes and may count shared pages more than once. Finished jobs have no live readings.

What are the current support limits?+

Foreground services on macOS and glibc-based Linux. No Windows, Docker management, auto-restart or arbitrary PID adoption. A descendant that creates a new group can escape cleanup. Use native VM storage for state; deadlines use wall time.
